Degree and Clustering Coefficient Centrality

Source: R/centrality-batch67.R
centrality_dcc.Rd

Degree and clustering coefficient centrality (DCC; Yang et al. 2020) adds a degree term and a clustering term, weighted by the entropy weight method: $$DCC(i) = \alpha I_D(i) + \beta I_C(i), \qquad I_D(i) = k_i + \sum_{j \in N(i)} k_j, \qquad I_C(i) = e^{-C_i} \sum_{j \in N_2(i)} C_j,$$ with \(k\) the degree, \(C\) the local clustering coefficient and \(N_2(i)\) the nodes within two steps of \(i\). Each attribute is divided by its Euclidean norm over the nodes, \(E_1\) and \(E_2\) are the entropies of the results divided by \(\ln n\), and \(\alpha = (1 - E_1) / (2 - E_1 - E_2)\), \(\beta = 1 - \alpha\).

Usage

centrality_dcc(x, ...)

Arguments

x

Network input accepted by centrality.

...

Further arguments to centrality, such as normalized.

Value

A named numeric vector with one score per node, in input node order.

Details

The measure is computed on the simple undirected skeleton of the network, so direction, weights, loops and parallel edges are ignored. \(N_2(i)\) holds the nodes one or two steps away: the clustering sum the source prints for node 8 of its Fig. 1(b), and its karate top five, need that reading; the Centrality Zoo says exactly two steps. The clustering coefficient is 0 below degree 2. The weights are computed for each network, so adding a component changes every score. On a network without a triangle the clustering term is 0 at every node and the entropy weights are 0/0; the measure then warns (class cograph_undefined_measure) and returns NA. It does the same when the two entropies add up to 2, where the weights divide by zero. The implementation reproduces the karate top five of the source's Table 3 and the share of tied scores of its Table 2 (32.35 percent). The source's worked example on its Fig. 1(b) prints 23 numbers: the 14 attribute values among them follow from the network drawn there, but its normalised attributes, its entropy, its weight \(\alpha\) and its score of node 1 (16.2677) do not. The printed entropy weights cannot be reproduced from the printed network; the score of node 1 here is 15.7429. On four test networks the score ranks nodes closest to diffusion and the two-step expected influence (mean Kendall correlation 0.94) and to centrality_semilocal (0.88 to 0.96). normalized = TRUE divides the scores by their maximum.

References

Yang, Y., Wang, X., Chen, Y., Hu, M. and Ruan, C. (2020). A novel centrality of influential nodes identification in complex networks. IEEE Access, 8, 58742-58751. doi:10.1109/ACCESS.2020.2983053 .

See also

centrality_semilocal, centrality_transitivity, centrality_degree, centrality.

Examples

centrality_dcc(to_undirected(regulation_net))
#>    Explore       Plan    Monitor      Adapt    Reflect    Discuss Synthesize 
#>   17.23582   20.28402   23.18891   20.02044   17.09047   17.90136   15.23920 
#>   Evaluate     Create      Share 
#>   18.73328   20.67871   18.58562
